tagline: A cloud-free voice assistant's local knowledge graph and diary memory

scenes.narration: Day 50: Jarvis, a voice assistant that needs no cloud AI.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: Desktop assistant run entirely on local models
Diary records what happened, a knowledge graph records what it learned
No tool calls needed: memory loads straight into the system prompt
scenes.narration: Jarvis runs only on local models. It keeps two memories: a diary of what happened, and a knowledge graph of what it learned.

steps.narration: A cheap local check first asks: does the current conversation already cover this? No model call needed.
If not, the diary searches past conversations, while the graph holds durable facts under three branches: user, directives, world.
Each branch grows as a tree. Past fifteen hundred tokens, a model splits a node and merges contradicting facts.
Results land straight in the system prompt for the next reply, no extra tool call needed.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Knowledge-graph evals passed on gemma4:e4b, run locally with Ollama on one GPU.
scenes.narration: On a local GPU with Ollama, all fifty-one knowledge graph evals passed. When we said we moved from Tokyo to Osaka, the graph rewrote the old fact, yet reported zero facts stored.
The Zenn article has the full logs and the no-mock demo scripts. Free for non-commercial use; source on GitHub.
